### 4. Safety performance review — SPI / SPT

The Board reviewed the two indicators tabled for the quarter. The SPIs themselves (definitions, alert/target levels) are maintained under the operator's SPI/SPT framework; the SRB reviews performance against them and directs action — it does not itself re-derive the indicators.

| Ref | Safety Performance Indicator | Type | Owning hazard / objective | Alert level (qtr) | Target level | Q2 2026 actual | Status | Trend |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SPI-01 | Unstabilised approaches continued to landing (count) | **Leading** | Unstable approach → runway excursion / CFIT *[ASSUMPTION — mapping inferred]* | 8 | *[GAP — not supplied]* | **12** | ⚠ **ALERT LEVEL BREACHED** | *[GAP — prior-quarter baseline not supplied]* |
| SPI-02 | Runway excursion events | **Lagging** | Runway excursion | *[GAP]* | *[GAP]* | *[GAP — reported at/within target]* | ✔ **AT TARGET** | Stable (per report; underlying values *[GAP]*) |

**4.1 SPI-01 — Unstabilised approaches (leading): ALERT BREACHED.**
The Board noted **12 exceedances against an alert level of 8** for the quarter — the alert threshold is exceeded and the indicator is in its alert region. As a **leading precursor** to runway excursion / CFIT, this is an early-warning signal that warrants a mandatory management response under the Safety Assurance pillar, **notwithstanding** that the related lagging outcome (SPI-02) remains at target. The Board did not accept the breach as within normal variation: a structured deep-dive was directed (see §5 / ACT-2026-Q2-01). The prior-quarter baseline and in-quarter trend were not tabled and are flagged **[GAP]** for the deep-dive to establish.

**4.2 SPI-02 — Runway excursion events (lagging): at target.**
The Board noted the runway-excursion lagging SPI **remained at target** for the quarter, with no breach. The Board recorded that a favourable lagging outcome does **not** offset an alerting leading indicator, and directed continued monitoring only (no additional action). Underlying event count and target value were not tabled **[GAP]** and should be attached to the record for completeness.

### 5. Hazard and risk decision — bird strike on departure

**5.1 Hazard reviewed.** Bird strike on departure (take-off / initial climb).

**5.2 Current risk classification (as tabled).** The Board acted on the current hazard-register rating of **Hazardous / Occasional → risk index 4B** on the ICAO 5×5 Risk Classification Scheme. On the ICAO tolerability scale, **4B falls in the intolerable (red) region** — a risk that is *unacceptable under existing circumstances* and must be reduced before the associated operation can be regarded as tolerable.¹ The SRB records this rating; it does not re-score it (scoring is owned by the hazard register).

**5.3 Discussion.** The existing control is a **crew briefing card** — an **administrative control** and, in isolation, low on the hierarchy of controls. The Board's position: an administrative-only control **cannot** reduce an intolerable-region (4B) risk to the tolerable region, and relying on the briefing card alone would not survive an audit of the risk-treatment rationale. Higher-order controls are therefore required, not optional.

**5.4 Decision.** The Board **accepted (endorsed) the risk-treatment plan to move beyond the briefing-card control** and directed its development and implementation (ACT-2026-Q2-02). The plan is to work up the hierarchy of controls; the briefing card is **retained as a backup administrative layer, not the primary control**.

**5.5 Treatment plan — hierarchy-of-controls workstreams.** *[ASSUMPTION — specific measures below are the endorsed shape of the plan for the accountable owner to detail and cost; they are not yet approved individual controls. Detailed re-scoring is routed to the hazard register.]*

| HoC tier | Candidate control for the plan | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| Elimination / Substitution | Not reasonably practicable (wildlife source not within operator control) | Retained as N/A with justification |
| Engineering / source reduction | Formal engagement with the **aerodrome operator's wildlife-hazard-management** programme (habitat management, dispersal, patrols, activity data-sharing) via the airport wildlife committee | Highest practicable tier for an operator; source-side |
| Operational / procedural | SOP amendments for high bird-activity windows (seasonal/time-of-day departure planning, use of lights/radar, thrust and speed-schedule considerations, wildlife-activity awareness in dispatch) | Substantive, above administrative |
| Training | Enhanced crew training on bird-strike avoidance and post-strike handling | Above briefing-card |
| Administrative (retained backup) | Strengthened crew briefing card, reinforced bird-strike reporting | The control being *moved beyond*, kept as backstop |

**5.6 Target residual.** The plan is to be developed with an explicit **target residual risk index in the tolerable (yellow) region**, subject to re-assessment in the hazard register and reported back to the next SRB. The Board did **not** accept 4B as a tolerated residual; it accepted a *plan to reduce it*.

¹ ICAO 5×5 Risk Classification Scheme (Annex 19 / Doc 9859, *Safety Management Manual*): likelihood 5 Frequent → 1 Extremely improbable; severity A Catastrophic → E Negligible. Tolerability regions — **intolerable/red:** 5A, 5B, 5C, 4A, **4B**, 3A; **tolerable/yellow:** 4C–4E, 5D–5E, 3B–3D, 2A–2C, 1A; **acceptable/green:** 3E, 2D–2E, 1B–1E. "Alert level" is the abnormal-performance trigger for an SPI; "target level" is the desired performance objective — the two are distinct.
